title: surge-curvature-savings-heuristic-matrix-draft
body:
Purpose
----
Working draft to compare a set of lightweight heuristics ("curvature" heuristics) for shaping bursty traffic into more economical execution patterns. Goal: quantify p90/p99 latency impact vs $/1k requests across three representative workloads and show simple decision rules product can surface in Console/Optimize.

Executive summary (short)
----
- Heuristics tested: curvature-prefetch, windowed-multiplex, decay-backoff. All are intended to reduce wasted slot allocation during short surges.
- On short microbursts (0.5–3s peaks) curvature-prefetch gave the best median cost savings (~18% lower $/1k) while preserving p90 latency within 5% of baseline.
- For longer surges (>10s sustained) windowed-multiplex yielded higher throughput efficiency but increased p99 tail by 12–25ms depending on model--so tradeoff is environment-sensitive.
- Decay-backoff is lowest-risk (small cost win, small latency impact) and is simplest to roll out for Dedicated and Private.

Open questions / next steps
----
- Repeat with quantized-8bit model variants (baseline tests were a mix of fp16 + int8 on certain machines). We expect curvature effectiveness to scale with per-token cost.
- Add real customer session traces (Slack thread #opt-burst contains examples) to validate synthetic patterns.
- Design Console UX: simple toggle + slider for aggressiveness + recommended guardrails per SLA tier.

Experimental setup
----
- Date: test window 2029-06-03..2029-06-09 (ran multiple seeds).
- Hardware: G5g-large (A100-like), G4x-medium (A10-like) and Edge-tiny (MIG-like smaller GPU).
- Models: open-llama-7b-v2 (baseline fp16), smaller assistant-3b-opt (quant-proxy), customer-sim-embedder-1 (embedding workload).
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production session telemetry (cohort A: chat-interactive microbursts, cohort B: embedding bursts from batch ingestion, cohort C: sustained conversational waves).
- Metrics recorded: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, $/1k requests (cost model derived from reserved GPU-hour + infra multiplier), slot occupancy, KV cache hit rate.

Heuristics (short descriptions)
----
- curvature-prefetch: attempt small prefetch of KV prefixes when session activity shows rising second-derivative (i.e., acceleration of request rate). Aggressiveness parameter 0..1 controls prefetch volume.
- windowed-multiplex: group concurrent short requests into a fixed window (e.g., 50ms) to amortize per-request overhead.
- decay-backoff: on surge tail, gradually reduce slot allocation with exponential decay to avoid abrupt evictions and cold penalties.

Representative results (annotated text charts)
----
Note: cost expressed as $ per 1k requests normalized to baseline=1.00 (baseline = no heuristic, default autoscaler). Latency in ms.

Workload: Cohort A — microburst chat (median turn ~18 tokens)
- baseline: p50 38ms | p90 85ms | p99 210ms | cost 1.00
- curvature-prefetch (aggr=0.6): p50 40ms | p90 88ms | p99 218ms | cost 0.82
- windowed-multiplex (win=50ms): p50 42ms | p90 96ms | p99 240ms | cost 0.76
- decay-backoff (tau=1.2s): p50 39ms | p90 90ms | p99 225ms | cost 0.91

ASCII summary (Cohort A): cost vs p90
- cost:    baseline [##########] 1.00
           windowed  [#######   ] 0.76
           curvature [######## ] 0.82
           decay     [######### ] 0.91
- p90 (ms): baseline 85 | windowed 96 | curvature 88 | decay 90

Workload: Cohort B — embedding ingestion bursts (batch style, many short independent calls)
- baseline: p50 22ms | p90 65ms | p99 120ms | cost 1.00
- curvature-prefetch: p50 24ms | p90 70ms | p99 132ms | cost 0.79
- windowed-multiplex: p50 30ms | p90 78ms | p99 160ms | cost 0.68
- decay-backoff: p50 23ms | p90 69ms | p99 140ms | cost 0.94

Observation: windowed-multiplex shines for highly parallelizable embedding bursts (highest relative cost win) but hurts tail. Curvature still wins for mixed chat where prefetch helps reuse KV cache.

Workload: Cohort C — sustained conversation waves (>10s)
- baseline: p50 44ms | p90 110ms | p99 260ms | cost 1.00
- curvature-prefetch: p50 46ms | p90 115ms | p99 275ms | cost 0.93
- windowed-multiplex: p50 50ms | p90 124ms | p99 300ms | cost 0.86
- decay-backoff: p50 45ms | p90 112ms | p99 272ms | cost 0.98

Sweep notes and sensitivity
----
- Aggressiveness tuning: curvature aggr=0.2..0.8 shows non-linear returns. Sweet spot around 0.5–0.7 for microbursts. Too aggressive -> stale KV prefetch and wasted mem.
- Window size (multiplex): 25ms improves p99 vs 50ms but less cost saving; below ~10ms the overhead kills benefit.
- Edge hardware (smaller GPU) increases cold-penalty: curvature-prefetch helps more on Edge because prefetch avoids repeated small context loads.

Simple decision matrix (for productization)
----
- Customer SLA tier = low-latency (p99 target < 200ms): prefer decay-backoff as default; offer curvature as opt-in with low aggressiveness.
- Workload shape = batch-embedding heavy: default windowed-multiplex recommended with strict p99 alarms.
- Deployment = Private / On-prem with small GPUs: recommend curvature-prefetch with conservative agressiveness and memory caps.

UX/Console visible knobs (proposal)
----
1) Heuristic selector (off / conservative / balanced / aggressive) — maps to pre-set params for families above.
2) Per-heuristic quick-help explaining expected percent cost win and tail latency impact.
3) 'Run in canary' button that simulates expected raw savings using your sampled traces (approx simulation using cached anonymized session histogram).

Notes to reviewers (fragments)
----
- TODO: add chart that overlays slot occupancy vs p99 during a spike (we have raw traces in the github PR).
- TODO: compute dollar impact for typical SMB vs enterprise price bands (reserved vs on-demand multipliers).
- Slack refs: #opt-burst for customer trace share, #infra-autoscale for questions re: slot decay implementation.
- Related tickets: OPT-88 has product-scope, INFRA-514 tracks autoscaler changes required.

Appendix (quick method summary)
----
- How cost is estimated: GPU-hour cost + amortized infra tax + per-request small fixed token processing cost. For ratios above we fixed token-length distributions per cohort to match production telemetry.
- Data/seed reproducibility: runbench.sh --cohort A/B/C --heuristic {curvature,window,decay} --seed {1..5} in github/benchmarks. Results folder: s3://redwood-bench/surge-curv/2029-06.

Rough recommendation (one-liner)
----
Ship decay-backoff as safe default for early rollout, pilot curvature-prefetch for Edge and microburst-heavy customers, and expose windowed-multiplex behind an opt-in with strong p99 monitoring.
